sources.title: Public model roster
sources.evidence: Fetched the live unauthenticated roster. Exact vispark/vision-medium has name Vispark: Vision Medium, owned_by vispark, 1,000,000 context, text/image/audio/video/file inputs, text output, and reasoning/tools features. Its created timestamp is May 15, 2024, but this is model metadata, not an explicit exact-variant release announcement.

sources.title: Vision playground and API documentation
sources.evidence: Read the deployed site and its current script index-g5phCnAo.js. Vision offers small, medium and large selectors, an authenticated paid API, optional continual-learning state, function tools and text/image/audio/video/PDF input. It specifies 1M context and separately limits combined input content to 980,000 tokens. The weights field carries learned session state; the site does not distribute the base checkpoint.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 model family table
sources.evidence: Current first-party homepage explicitly labels Vision CLv1 Medium as 175B, separately from 550B full and 45B small. The model is presented with a proprietary continual-learning core. Playground links lead to the same Vispark Lab service.

sources.title: Continual Learning Models: An Introduction to Weight Management
sources.evidence: Read the complete indexed primary article, crawled approximately one month before review; direct web and HTTP fetches timed out. Section 3 describes a modified Transformer. Section 5 states three models were trained on that architecture; section 6 explicitly lists Vision CLv1 Medium (175B) and says all three are live at Vispark Lab. No active count or dense/MoE classification is given. These are later CLv1 specifications, not proof of the original 2024 model configuration or of authenticated inference operation.

sources.title: Vision AI by Vispark: a foundational Indian multimodal AI
sources.evidence: September 1, 2025 article explicitly offers the API in small, medium and large sizes. Establishes that the Medium product was publicly available by this date, but does not state its first release date. Confirms the Vision family and text/image/audio/video/PDF inputs.

sources.title: Vispark product timeline
sources.evidence: Read the timeline in deployed script index-BgxKNlqk.js. May 15, 2024 is generic Vision chat launch on vansh.one, May 15, 2025 a chat relaunch, and August 29, 2025 the Lab platform launch. None explicitly dates the first release of the Medium variant.

sources.title: Terms of Service, September 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Read the terms in the current deployed site script. Section 2 covers AI tools and other platform services. Section 5 reserves service content, features and functionality to Vispark and licensors and restricts copying, distribution and modification without written consent. Supports descriptive proprietary hosted access; this is not a public model-weight license.

sources.title: A Culturally Aware Multimodal AI Model, July 2024
sources.evidence: Primary paper describes generic Vision with 175B parameters and a decoder-only Transformer. It does not identify a Medium size. Its identical numerical count is not the basis for the current Medium count, and its image-generation output is not transferred to the current text-output endpoint.

sources.title: A Self-Improving Experiential AI Model a Path to Continual Learning, November 2025
sources.evidence: Primary report describes generic Vision Experiential at 250B and an earlier 175B Vision base, without a Medium variant label. No active count is disclosed. Neither count nor detailed architecture is transferred to the exact current Medium endpoint.

sources.title: Vision CLv1 evaluation harness
sources.evidence: Repository linked from the CLv1 article identifies its model as Vispark/Vision and supports the small/medium/large size API, with medium used for analysis calls. Confirms the same service identity. Its MIT license applies to the evaluation code, not to model weights.

name.note: Exact API model name with the provider prefix omitted for display; CLv1 Medium is the later documented generation.

developer.note: Exact endpoint is owned by Vispark. Later AIVOCO material identifies the same Vision model family and directs users to Vispark Lab; preserve the established catalog developer label.

family.note: The developer explicitly groups small, medium and large under Vision; later generation is labeled CLv1.

release_date.note: May 15, 2024 is a generic Vision chat launch and a created metadata value, not verified first availability of Medium. Exact three-size API access is documented by September 1, 2025; August 29 only establishes the Lab launch. First Medium release and CLv1 alias transition dates remain unresolved.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is authenticated hosted inference, with a proprietary core and restricted service rights. No base checkpoint is offered by these exact-model sources. Downloadable continual-learning state is not the full base weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted model under reserved service rights. Research-paper CC-BY and evaluation-code MIT licenses do not license the model checkpoint.

parameters_b.note: Nominal author-reported count for the later Vision CLv1 Medium offered at the same Vispark Lab medium selector. The API roster does not expose a dated checkpoint, so this is the latest documented alias specification, not a reconstructed original-release count. It is not inferred from the older generic 175B Vision paper or independently counted tensors.

active_parameters_b.note: No separately stated active count found in exact CLv1 Medium disclosures or the inspected earlier technical reports. Total parameters are not equated with active parameters.

architecture.note: The CLv1 article explicitly describes modified Transformer architecture and says all three models, including Medium, were trained on it. Dense/MoE structure, layer layout and detailed computation remain undisclosed. This describes the later CLv1 alias state.

context_window.note: Exact live roster specifies 1,000,000 tokens. Native documentation separately limits combined input content to 980,000 tokens; this does not reduce the advertised context field.

modalities.note: Exact endpoint outputs text; roster file input is resolved as PDF by the native playground documentation. Separate image/audio generation services are not model outputs here.

reasoning.note: Exact current endpoint advertises reasoning in supported_features. This is a documented capability, not an independently tested reasoning quality result or an assertion of a visible reasoning channel.

tool_call.note: Exact endpoint advertises tools; native developer documentation supplies function definitions and tool-call protocol for the Medium size.

description.value: Medium-size Vision model served through Vispark Lab, accepting text, image, audio, video and PDF inputs and returning text, with reasoning and tool calling.
description.note: Replaces balanced/deeper reasoning promotional claims with documented modality, access and capabilities.

patch.description: Medium-size Vision model served through Vispark Lab, accepting text, image, audio, video and PDF inputs and returning text, with reasoning and tool calling.

sources.label: Continual Learning Models: An Introduction to Weight Management
Vision AI by Vispark: a foundational Indian multimodal AI

patch.notes: 175B is the nominal developer-reported total for the later Vision CLv1 Medium served at Vispark Lab; its architecture is described as a modified Transformer. The API alias has no published dated checkpoint or transition history, so these specifications are not backdated to 2024. Active parameters and dense/MoE structure remain undisclosed. The upstream May 15, 2024 date is a generic Vision launch and model-created metadata; Medium API availability is explicit by September 1, 2025, but its first release date is unresolved. The context is 1,000,000 tokens, with a separate 980,000-token combined-input limit. Continual-learning state files are not publicly released base weights.

summary: Added later CLv1 Medium nominal 175B total and modified Transformer architecture, Vision family and supported proprietary classification. Confirmed exact endpoint context, modalities, reasoning and tools. Cleared unsupported exact release date and rewrote the description. Active count and detailed network structure remain undisclosed; CLv1 alias transition and initial Medium release remain unresolved.
